newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 rubber import needs seen at 31,000 tns.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 rubber import needs seen at 31,000 tns.

text.p: India will need to import 31,000 tonnes of rubber in 1996/97 (April-March) in order to meet projected consumption, according to the state-run Rubber Board's estimates presented at conference here on Sunday.

The Rubber Board estimated production in 1996/97 (April-March) at 547,000 tonnes against consumption of 578,000 tonnes, an official of the state run board told the United Planters Association of Southern India annual conference at this southern hill town.
Rubber Board Chairman K.J. Mathew said a decision on the quantum of additional imports will be taken around February next year.
Mathew estimated the gap between production and demand will widen to 60,000 tonnes by the year 2002, and 300,000 by 2010 unless an additional 36,000 hectares a year were brought under cultivation.
"We must produce 1.28 million tonnes by 2010 by bringing 36,000 hectares of land under rubber cultivation over the next 10 years," he told the conference.
